subject: Renewal: Catena dedicated expansion + proposed SLA addendum
messages:
From: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@catena-ht.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@catena-ht.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion next week

Sean / Marissa —

Thanks for kicking this off. As we discussed in the call, our primary ask for the renewal is to secure a dedicated pool that supports an additional 16 GPUs (NVIDIA H100 equivalent) and a throughput baseline of ~1.2M tokens/day with predictable p99 latency under 220ms for the 4k-context models.

Two items to confirm for our procurement team:
- Will Redwood accept a 24-month term with quarterly billing?
- We need a written SLA addendum that captures latency SLOs and the credits structure if p99 or uptime targets are missed — procurement will not sign without explicit credit math.

I attached a short workbook describing current usage and peaks. Happy to talk tomorrow.

—Jared
Catena HealthTech
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@catena-ht.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion next week

Jared —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front:
- 24-month term with quarterly billing — yes, we can do that.
- We can propose an SLA addendum with explicit credit tiers for both uptime and latency breaches, but we will need to request a limited SLA exception for the first 60 days after expansion while we finalize canary routing and KV cache warm-up behavior.

What that exception means in practice: we guarantee the baseline throughput and will provision the additional reserved GPUs at contract start, but we ask for a 60-day operational window where latency SLOs are monitored and performance credits are on a capped schedule (we can propose a pro-rated credit formula). This protects both sides while we tune batching/quant profiles to your workload.

Marissa — can you attach the proposal and an SLA draft? Neha / Rishi — loop in any legal/compliance items we should surface.

Thanks,
Sean
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@catena-ht.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Catena renewal proposal + SLA addendum (draft)

Jared — attaching proposal v2 and an SLA addendum draft. Highlights:
- Reserved pool: +16 GPUs (H100 equiv), initial allocation day 1.
- Baseline throughput target: 1.2M tokens/day; burst capacity up to 1.6M tokens/day (subject to autoscale policies).
- Latency SLO: p99 < 220ms for defined 4k endpoint.
- 60-day tuning window: during this period, latency credits are capped at 50% of normal credit exposure; after 60 days, standard credit formula applies.
- Fallback: we will route to a compatible lower-cost variant if we detect sustained capacity issues; customers get 90 days of data export rights if they choose to terminate early for breaches.

Request: Please confirm whether procurement needs different wording on credits (percentage/rate). Also, confirm billing cadence.

Attachments: Catena_Renewal_Proposal_v2.pdf (proposal workbook), SLA_Addendum_Draft.docx (track changes on margins)

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@catena-ht.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@catena-ht.com>, procurement@catena-ht.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Catena renewal proposal + SLA addendum (draft)

Thanks Marissa — quick notes from procurement: the 60-day tuning window is acceptable in principle, but we need clearer credit math. Specifically:
- Credit tiers tied to monthly uptime % (99.95% / 99.5% / 99.0%) and p99 latency bands (>220ms, >300ms) with explicit dollar credits per hour/minute of breach.
- We cannot accept a hard cap that reduces our maximum credit below 30% of the monthly invoice for severe outages.
- Can you confirm how fallbacks to lower-cost model variants will impact contractual throughput guarantees? Procurement wants an explicit statement that routing to fallbacks will not count as a breach if it was automated during a region-wide capacity event.

Also, legal will want to see language on data residency and audit logs for the reserved pool.

—Marta
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@catena-ht.com>, Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@catena-ht.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Catena renewal proposal + SLA addendum (draft)

Marta —

Thanks for the clear feedback. Rishi and I reviewed procurement's asks and here are our proposed updates to the SLA addendum (summary):
- Credit math: explicit dollar-per-hour formula for each tier: 99.95% = $0/hr, 99.5% = 5% monthly invoice/hr of breach, 99.0% = 15% monthly invoice/hr of breach. Latency breaches: first threshold (>220ms p99) triggers notification; second threshold (>300ms p99) triggers partial credit at 2%/hour; extreme (>500ms) escalates to full outage credit computations. We will include worked examples in the doc.
- 60-day tuning window: during day 0-60 we will calculate credits but cap cumulative credits at 50% of the normal max; after day 60 full-credit exposure applies. We can move the cap floor to 30% if Catena requires — willing to negotiate.
- Fallback behavior: routing to pre-agreed compatible model variants during a region event will not count as a breach; we will document the conditions (automated health checks + front-run mitigation).
- Data residency & audit logs: reserved pool will be provisioned in us-west-2 region; we will provide KMS-backed logs and weekly export for the contract duration.

Rishi — can you confirm wording for the credit percentages and the legal hold language?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@catena-ht.com>, Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@catena-ht.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Catena renewal proposal + SLA addendum (draft)

Marta / Jared —

Putting this in legalese for the addendum: we will include three uptime tiers with explicit per-hour credit multipliers tied to monthly invoice amounts, and a latency-credit schedule as Neha summarized. For the initial 60-day operational window, credits will be both calculated and visible (via the Console) but the maximum exposure will be capped at 40% of the standard maximum credit calculation (we propose 40% as a middle ground). If Catena prefers 30%, we can accept that with an escalation clause tying the cap to a post-60-day review.

Next steps: Marissa to incorporate these numbers into SLA_Addendum_Draft.docx and return to procurement with a tracked-changes copy. Sean / Marissa to schedule a short call with Catena procurement & legal on Thursday to finalize language prior to countersign.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
